questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your side mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure it is safe.

questions.question: Work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used to:

options.text: Make drivers angry about slow traffic.
Keep traffic out of hazardous work zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep traffic out of hazardous work zones.
questions.explanation: Work zones are dangerous for both workers and drivers. Cones, barrels, signs, and workers in bright vests warn you and direct traffic away from the danger.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: You should speed up so you can make the turn before the light changes.
You do not need to signal to turn from the indicated lane.
You should prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the green arrow protection is ending. If you are turning in that direction, prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic before turning.

questions.question: Before you enter an intersection, you should look to your:
questions.explanation: Before entering an intersection, look left and right for vehicles and pedestrians. Look left a second time because vehicles from your left will be closer. Check that the path is clear all the way through.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that wet roads are slippery and dangerous. Slow down on wet pavement because it takes longer to stop.

questions.question: If a traffic signal is green but a police officer signals you to stop, what should you do?

options.text: Do what the vehicle in front of you does.

questions.explanation: You must obey a police officer's instructions, even if they contradict traffic signals, signs, or road markings.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a left turn. It is unsafe and illegal to turn left where this sign is posted.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, what should you do?
questions.explanation: When being passed, keep your speed steady and yield to the passing vehicle. Do not speed up or brake. Let the vehicle safely merge back into your lane.

questions.question: If you have had several beers, how can the effects of alcohol be reduced?
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Coffee, exercise, or cold showers do not speed up this process. It takes about one hour for your body to process one drink.

questions.question: The maximum posted speed limit should be driven only:
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the fastest legal speed only when conditions are ideal. Drive at the same speed as surrounding traffic, up to the maximum limit. Safe speed is every driver's responsibility.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle, you must yield by:

options.text: Moving to the right edge of the road and stopping.
Speeding up to clear the lane.
Moving to the right lane and driving slowly until it passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Moving to the right edge of the road and stopping.
questions.explanation: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle, move to the right edge of the road as far as possible. Stop and wait for the emergency vehicle to pass. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first before stopping.

questions.question: Like alcohol and drugs, drowsiness can:
questions.explanation: Not getting enough sleep causes poor driving. Drowsiness slows your reaction time, reduces your awareness, and hurts your judgment—just like alcohol and drugs.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to dangers ahead. This sign warns that you are leaving a one-way highway and entering a two-way highway.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle when:

options.text: You are on a hill or curve.
You are on a road with a solid line next to your lane.
You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.
questions.explanation: A broken line means you can cross it to change lanes. Solid yellow lines mean you cannot pass. Only change lanes when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Last turn before a toll road.

questions.explanation: Orange signs mark work zones. This sign warns you that a flagger is ahead. You must follow the flagger's directions.

questions.question: Which is dangerous in a work zone?

options.text: Not watching carefully for workers and equipment.

questions.explanation: In a work zone, slow down and keep distance from other vehicles. Watch carefully for workers and equipment.

questions.question: Work zone traffic control devices are which color?
questions.explanation: Orange signs, cones, and barriers mark work zones. Use extra caution when you see them.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Orange diamond signs mark construction and maintenance areas. Fines for traffic violations double in these zones.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A triangle pointing down is always a yield sign. Slow down or stop when you see it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns of a steep hill ahead. Slow down and shift to a lower gear to protect your brakes.

questions.question: Fatigue increases the risk of:

options.text: Falling asleep while driving and crashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Falling asleep while driving and crashing.
questions.explanation: Fatigue slows your reaction time and decision-making. You could fall asleep behind the wheel and crash, which can injure or kill you or others.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You cannot turn around to go in the opposite direction at this location.

questions.question: You are driving on the freeway behind a large truck. You should drive:

options.text: Closer behind the truck than you would a passenger vehicle.
Farther behind the truck than you would a passenger vehicle.
To the right side of the truck and wait to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther behind the truck than you would a passenger vehicle.
questions.explanation: Drive farther behind a large truck than a passenger vehicle. Large trucks have bigger blind spots, so you need more distance to stay safe.

questions.question: Tailgating other drivers (driving too close to their rear bumper):

options.text: Can frustrate other drivers and make them angry.
Cannot result in a traffic ticket.
Reduces crashes by preventing being cut off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can frustrate other drivers and make them angry.
questions.explanation: Tailgating is a common dangerous behavior that can lead to aggressive driving. You can receive a traffic ticket for unsafe driving.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A five-sided yellow or yellow-green sign warns you of a school zone or school crossing.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A diamond-shaped yellow sign warns of possible danger ahead. Orange diamond-shaped signs warn of dangers in or near work zones.

questions.question: One vehicle that must stop at all railroad crossings is:
questions.explanation: School buses, transit buses, and vehicles carrying hazardous materials must stop at all railroad tracks before crossing. Be ready to stop when following these vehicles at railroad crossings.

questions.question: What is the only proven way to remove alcohol or drugs from your system?
questions.explanation: Cold showers, coffee, and exercise do not reduce alcohol in your blood. The only way to lower your blood alcohol level is to wait.

questions.question: Collisions are more likely to happen when:

options.text: All vehicles are traveling at about the same speed.
One lane of traffic is traveling faster than other lanes.
One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: Collisions happen more often when one driver goes faster or slower than other vehicles. Driving too fast or too slow increases crash risk and can cause other drivers to swerve to avoid you.

questions.question: Before changing lanes or passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Check your blind spots and mirrors.
Signal your intention before changing lanes.

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes to alert other drivers. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving your vehicle left or right.
